title: Spandeck Engineering (S) Pte Ltd v Defence Science & Technology Agency
body: The Court of Appeal considered the proper test for determining whether a duty of care exists in Singapore negligence law. The court adopted a single test applicable to all claims in negligence. A claimant must first show factual foreseeability. The court then considers legal proximity, including physical, circumstantial and causal proximity, before asking whether policy considerations negate or limit a prima facie duty. On the facts, the claim concerned economic loss arising from alleged defects in building works. The judgment explains that the inquiry remains fact-sensitive and incremental, with reference to decided cases. The court also addressed the relationship between contractual arrangements and tortious duties. The existence of a contract does not automatically exclude a duty in tort, but the contractual allocation of risk may affect proximity or policy.
